hypothesis.title: Pharmacological ERAP1 modulation as an axSpA intervention strategy (working formulation)
hypothesis.description: Pharmacological modulation of ERAP1 can alter HLA-B27-related antigen-processing biology in a direction relevant to axial spondyloarthritis in appropriate genetic and cellular contexts.
hypothesis.rationale: AXIS-drafted working formulation of the project objective; an AI suggestion pending researcher review, not an investigator-approved hypothesis.

explanations.label: On-target ERAP1 modulation
explanations.statement: The HLA-B27-related cellular phenotype produced by the compounds arises from direct modulation of ERAP1 in those cells.

explanations.label: Off-target activity
explanations.statement: The phenotype arises primarily from compound activity at targets other than ERAP1 (for example ERAP2 or unrelated proteins).

explanations.label: Indirect pathway
explanations.statement: ERAP1 is perturbed, but the HLA-B27-related phenotype arises through an indirect pathway rather than proximal catalytic modulation.

explanations.label: Context-dependent effect
explanations.statement: The effect depends on HLA-B27 subtype or ERAP1 allotype context rather than being a general consequence of ERAP1 modulation.

candidate_experiments.title: Matched-genotype chemical-genetic experiment with an engagement readout
candidate_experiments.rationale: Compare the compound in HLA-B27 cells with and without ERAP1, with ERAP1 re-expression, while measuring cellular engagement and the source-linked phenotype in the same system, so that attribution to ERAP1 can be tested directly.
candidate_experiments.experimental_system: HLA-B27-positive cell system with wild-type, ERAP1-depleted or null, and ERAP1-rescued arms in a matched genetic background
candidate_experiments.intervention_description: Compound at phenotype-active exposures versus vehicle and an inactive analogue in each arm; ERAP1 genetic depletion and re-expression as the genetic comparison.
candidate_experiments.endpoint_description: Cellular ERAP1 engagement and the source-linked HLA-B27 phenotype, measured separately with a viability readout.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
controls_negative: ERAP1-null or ERAP1-depleted arm of the same background
structurally related inactive analogue, if one is established (none identified in the curated corpus)
controls_positive: none established in the curated corpus; a reference ERAP1 ligand with demonstrated cellular engagement would be required
profile.primary_endpoint: Compound-dependent ERAP1 engagement at the exposures that produce the phenotype, together with phenotype attenuation in ERAP1-null cells
secondary_endpoints: cell viability at the tested exposures
restoration of phenotype after ERAP1 re-expression
limitations: Does not resolve selectivity against other proteins
Single cellular system; disease relevance and patient-derived cells are not addressed
A null or rescue model does not reproduce partial pharmacological inhibition
prerequisites: validated compound identity (the DG013A label is not resolved to one substance)

context_requirements.hla: HLA-B27 subtype to be chosen and reported

scenarios.outcome: Engagement is detected at phenotype-active exposures in wild-type cells; the phenotype is attenuated in ERAP1-null cells and restored by ERAP1 re-expression.
scenarios.interpretation: Compatible with ERAP1-dependent action at these exposures in this system.

on_target: Engagement and genetic dependence both align with the phenotype.
off_target: Phenotype requires ERAP1 and is restored by re-expression.
indirect_pathway: An indirect pathway downstream of ERAP1 is also ERAP1-dependent.
context_dependent: A single matched background does not test context.

consequence.statement: If engagement and ERAP1-dependence are both observed, the current evidence would support continuing the ERAP1 strategy for this compound in this context, with selectivity and context still to be addressed.

scenarios.outcome: Engagement is detected in wild-type cells, but the phenotype persists unchanged in ERAP1-null cells.
scenarios.interpretation: The phenotype does not require ERAP1 in this system.

on_target: The phenotype is independent of ERAP1.
off_target: A target-independent phenotype is the expected pattern of off-target action.
indirect_pathway: An ERAP1-dependent indirect pathway would also be lost in null cells.

consequence.statement: If the phenotype persists without ERAP1, the compound would no longer support an ERAP1-dependent strategy and alternative chemotypes would need their own engagement and dependency evidence.

scenarios.outcome: No engagement signal is detected in a validated assay, yet the phenotype is attenuated in ERAP1-null cells.
scenarios.interpretation: ERAP1 contributes, but not through detectable binding of this compound.

on_target: Direct modulation is not supported by the engagement assay.
indirect_pathway: ERAP1-dependent phenotype without direct engagement fits an indirect route.

consequence.statement: If the phenotype is ERAP1-dependent without detectable engagement, the mechanistic model would change toward an indirect route and the strategy would need re-justification.

scenarios.outcome: Engagement and ERAP1-dependence differ between HLA-B27 backgrounds or ERAP1 allotypes.
scenarios.interpretation: The result is context dependent.

consequence.statement: If engagement or dependence varies with background, the next evidence needed would be a matched allotype and HLA-B27 subtype comparison before any strategy decision.

scenarios.outcome: The null or rescue model is not validated, or toxicity confounds the phenotype.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference about engagement or dependence is permitted.

on_target: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
off_target: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
indirect_pathway: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
context_dependent: Technical failure is not a biological negative.

consequence.statement: If the experiment is non-interpretable, the uncertainty would remain open and the model and controls would need to be validated before repeating it.
consequence.new_uncertainty: validity of the null or rescue model

candidate_experiments.title: Cellular ERAP1 target-engagement measurement at phenotype-active exposures
candidate_experiments.rationale: Measure whether the compound engages ERAP1 in cells at the exposures that produce the reported HLA-B27 phenotype, using ERAP1-depleted cells as a specificity control.
candidate_experiments.experimental_system: HLA-B27-positive cell line with a matched ERAP1-depleted control
candidate_experiments.intervention_description: Compound concentration series spanning the phenotype-active exposures versus vehicle.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
controls_negative: ERAP1-depleted cells of the same background
controls_positive: none established in the curated corpus; a reference ERAP1 ligand with demonstrated cellular engagement would be required
profile.primary_endpoint: Compound-dependent ERAP1 engagement at phenotype-active exposures
limitations: Engagement does not show dependence of the phenotype on ERAP1
prerequisites: validated compound identity (the DG013A label is not resolved to one substance)

context_requirements.hla: HLA-B27 subtype to be chosen and reported

scenarios.outcome: Engagement is detected at phenotype-active exposures and is absent in ERAP1-depleted cells.
scenarios.interpretation: The compound reaches and binds ERAP1 in cells at these exposures.

off_target: Engagement does not exclude additional off-target contribution.
indirect_pathway: Engagement does not show proximal catalytic modulation.

consequence.statement: If engagement is detected, the current evidence would support on-target action at these exposures, but dependency and selectivity remain open and orthogonal validation would be required.

scenarios.outcome: No engagement at phenotype-active exposures in a validated assay.
scenarios.interpretation: The phenotype is unlikely to arise from direct engagement at these exposures.

off_target: Phenotype without engagement is the expected off-target pattern.
indirect_pathway: An indirect route through ERAP1 still requires ERAP1 modulation.

consequence.statement: If no engagement is detected in a validated assay, an on-target explanation for this compound's phenotype would be weakened and the compound would be a poor basis for the ERAP1 strategy.

scenarios.outcome: Engagement occurs only at exposures well above those producing the phenotype.
scenarios.interpretation: Phenotype and engagement are not aligned in exposure.

off_target: A more potent target is implied.

consequence.statement: If engagement requires far higher exposures than the phenotype, the mechanistic model would change and the phenotype would need another explanation.

scenarios.outcome: The assay fails its vehicle or positive-control criteria.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference about engagement is permitted.

on_target: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
off_target: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
indirect_pathway: Technical failure is not a biological negative.
context_dependent: Technical failure is not a biological negative.

consequence.statement: If the assay is non-interpretable, the uncertainty would remain open and the assay would need to be re-established before the question can be addressed.

candidate_experiments.title: Concentration-response alignment of engagement and phenotype
candidate_experiments.rationale: Measure engagement and the HLA-B27 phenotype across the same concentration series to test whether they align.
candidate_experiments.endpoint_description: Engagement and phenotype concentration-response curves in the same system.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
profile.primary_endpoint: Alignment of engagement and phenotype concentration-response
limitations: Does not test dependence on ERAP1
Requires the same engagement readout as a direct engagement measurement
prerequisites: validated compound identity (the DG013A label is not resolved to one substance)

scenarios.outcome: Engagement and phenotype concentration-response curves align.
scenarios.interpretation: Consistent with, but not proof of, engagement-driven phenotype.

off_target: Alignment does not exclude a co-potent off-target.

consequence.statement: If the curves align, the current evidence would support continued investigation, but alignment alone would not establish dependence and orthogonal validation would be required.

scenarios.outcome: The phenotype occurs at concentrations without detectable engagement.
scenarios.interpretation: Phenotype is not accounted for by engagement.

consequence.statement: If the phenotype occurs without engagement, an on-target explanation for the compound would be weakened.

scenarios.outcome: Assay sensitivity is inadequate to place engagement across the series.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference is permitted.

consequence.statement: If assay sensitivity is inadequate, the uncertainty would remain open and the assay would need to be improved before repeating.

candidate_experiments.title: Repeat the reported HLA-B27 phenotype with additional replicates
candidate_experiments.rationale: Repeat the source phenotype assay with more replicates to improve precision. It is listed because it is a common first impulse, not because it addresses engagement.
candidate_experiments.experimental_system: The system of the source study
candidate_experiments.intervention_description: Same compound and exposure as the source study.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
profile.primary_endpoint: Reproducibility of the reported surface phenotype
limitations: Does not measure engagement, dependence or selectivity
Every outcome weakens or leaves unchanged all compound-based explanations together
prerequisites: validated compound identity (the DG013A label is not resolved to one substance)

scenarios.outcome: The phenotype reproduces with the same direction and similar magnitude.
scenarios.interpretation: Improves confidence that the phenotype is reproducible; says nothing about its cause.

consequence.statement: If the phenotype reproduces, the current evidence would be unchanged with respect to ERAP1 attribution and the uncertainty about engagement would remain.

scenarios.outcome: The phenotype does not reproduce.
scenarios.interpretation: The original phenotype is not robust in this setting.

consequence.statement: If the phenotype does not reproduce, all compound-based explanations would weaken together and the original finding would need independent replication before any strategy decision.

scenarios.outcome: The assay fails its quality criteria.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference is permitted.

consequence.statement: If the assay is non-interpretable, nothing would change and the assay would need to be repeated.

candidate_experiments.title: Matched ERAP1 allotype and HLA-B27 subtype panel
candidate_experiments.rationale: Test whether the effect of ERAP1 perturbation depends on ERAP1 allotype and HLA-B27 subtype in matched isogenic backgrounds.
candidate_experiments.experimental_system: Isogenic cells expressing defined ERAP1 allotypes and HLA-B27 subtypes
candidate_experiments.intervention_description: The same ERAP1 perturbation across the allotype and subtype matrix.
candidate_experiments.endpoint_description: HLA-B27 surface phenotype and peptide-length distribution per context.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
profile.primary_endpoint: Direction and size of the phenotype across allotype and subtype
limitations: Isogenic systems are not patient cells
prerequisites: isogenic ERAP1 allotype and HLA-B27 subtype models

scenarios.outcome: Direction or magnitude of the effect varies by allotype or subtype.
scenarios.interpretation: The effect is context dependent.

consequence.statement: If the effect varies with background, the strategy would need to be defined per allotype and subtype before any further decision.

scenarios.outcome: The effect is consistent across the matched allotypes and subtypes.
scenarios.interpretation: The effect is general to ERAP1 perturbation in these contexts.

on_target: A general effect is compatible with a direct consequence of ERAP1 perturbation.
off_target: Genetic perturbation does not involve the compound.

consequence.statement: If the effect is consistent across contexts, the context uncertainty would be resolved for the current decision and compound-level engagement and dependence would become the limiting evidence.

scenarios.outcome: The panel is not isogenic or its expression levels differ.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference is permitted.

consequence.statement: If the panel is not matched, the context uncertainty would remain open and the panel would need to be rebuilt.

candidate_experiments.title: Chemically distinct ERAP1 probe at the same endpoint
candidate_experiments.rationale: Test whether a chemically distinct ERAP1 modulator with demonstrated engagement reproduces the phenotype, separating chemotype-specific off-target effects from target biology.
candidate_experiments.intervention_description: A second, structurally unrelated ERAP1 modulator versus the original compound.
candidate_experiments.endpoint_description: The same HLA-B27 surface phenotype with engagement measured.

profile.disease_relevance: molecular HLA-B27 context only; not disease rescue
controls_negative: inactive analogue of the second probe, if established
profile.primary_endpoint: Phenotype reproduced by a chemically distinct modulator with engagement
limitations: Requires a probe that does not yet exist in the curated corpus
Does not by itself show dependence on ERAP1
prerequisites: selective, chemically distinct ERAP1 probe with cellular engagement

scenarios.outcome: The distinct probe engages ERAP1 and reproduces the phenotype.
scenarios.interpretation: The phenotype tracks ERAP1 modulation across chemotypes.

off_target: A shared off-target is less likely.

consequence.statement: If a distinct probe with engagement reproduces the phenotype, the current evidence would support continuing the ERAP1 strategy across chemotypes.

scenarios.outcome: The distinct probe engages ERAP1 but does not reproduce the phenotype.
scenarios.interpretation: The phenotype is specific to the original chemotype.

consequence.statement: If a distinct engaged probe does not reproduce the phenotype, the original phenotype would be attributed to the chemotype and the ERAP1 strategy would be weakened.

scenarios.outcome: No probe meets the engagement criteria.
scenarios.interpretation: No inference is permitted.

consequence.statement: If no probe qualifies, the selectivity uncertainty would remain open and a suitable probe would need to be established first.
